records.quote: Example 2 Let (X1 , X2 , X3 ) and (Y1 ,Y2 ,Y3 ) be two sets of independent random variables such that each Xi follows the Log-LFR distribution with parameters αi and βi , and each Yi follows the Log-LFR distribution with parameters αi∗ and βi∗ , for i = 1, 2, 3. To validate the result established in Theorem 2, different sets of values for the parameter vectors (α1 , α2 , α3 ), (α1∗ , α2∗ , α3∗ ), (β1 , β2 , β3 ) and (β1∗ , β2∗ , β3∗ ) are considered for a fixed value of p > 0. The plot of the difference F̄Y1:3 (y) − F̄X1:3 (y) is presented in Figure 5 for various parameter configurations to visually demonstrate the stochastic ordering.

records.quote: Remark 1 The following result is well known in the literature (Shaked and Shanthikumar16 ): X ≤lr Y ⇒ X ≤hr Y ⇒ X ≤st Y. The relationship between these orderings follows a cascading pattern: likelihood ratio ordering establishes hazard rate ordering, which in turn generates the usual stochastic ordering. Consequently, under the conditions stated in Theorem 1, the hazard rate and usual stochastic naturally follow from the likelihood ratio ordering.
